# Chiang Mai Solo Wellness Retreat Plan

A calm 3-day retreat built around slow mornings, one massage, one easy nature walk, vegetarian meals, and low-cost indoor backups.
Budget target: **$450 total excluding airfare**; this plan stays comfortably under that.

## 3-Day Wellness Itinerary and Cost Plan

| Day | Focus | Main Plan | Estimated Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sep 18 | Arrival + reset | Gentle check-in, temple stroll, sunset tea, early night | **$85** |
| Sep 19 | Nature + massage | Easy hike, vegetarian lunch, Thai massage, quiet café time | **$145** |
| Sep 20 | Slow close | Sunrise meditation, market breakfast, journaling, departure buffer | **$95** |

### Day 1: Settle In and Decompress
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/moon-stars.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, unpack, and take a short walk near your stay to reset after travel.
- Afternoon: Visit a quiet temple or garden, then rest with herbal tea and a book.
- Evening: Vegetarian dinner at a calm café, then an early night.
- Estimated costs: lodging **$40**, meals **$20**, local transport **$10**, tea/snacks **$5**, buffer **$10**

### Day 2: Easy Hike and Massage
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Do an easy hike or nature walk at an accessible spot such as a gentle forest trail or hill temple area.
- Afternoon: Vegetarian lunch, then a **60–90 minute Thai massage** for recovery.
- Evening: Quiet café or spa lounge time, light dinner, journaling, and no late plans.
- Estimated costs: lodging **$40**, meals **$25**, transport **$15**, massage **$25–$40**, entrance/guide **$5–$15**, buffer **$10**

### Day 3: Slow Finish and Departure
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- Morning: Sunrise meditation, light stretching, and a slow vegetarian breakfast.
- Afternoon: Optional artisan market or a final temple stop, then pack and check out.
- Evening: Departure or one last simple meal before leaving.
- Estimated costs: lodging **$35**, meals **$20**, transport **$10**, snacks/water **$5**, buffer **$10**

## Budget Snapshot and Backup Rain Options

| Category | Planned Spend | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Lodging | **$115** | Quiet guesthouse, boutique hostel private room, or simple wellness stay |
| Meals | **$65** | Vegetarian cafés, temple-area rice dishes, fruit, tea |
| Transport | **$35** | Grab/tuk-tuk for short hops; mostly walkable days |
| Massage | **$25–$40** | One Thai massage session, off-peak pricing possible |
| Activities | **$20** | Temple entry, trail fees, small donations |
| Rain backup | **$25** | Museum, café, co-working day pass, indoor studio class |
| Cushion | **$70–$90** | Extra flexibility for upgrades or weather changes |

### Heavy-Rain Backup Activities
- Quiet café day with journaling, reading, and herbal tea
- Thai cooking class focused on vegetarian dishes
- Spa circuit: foot massage, sauna, or aromatherapy treatment
- Museum or cultural center visit
- Indoor yoga, stretching, or guided breathwork session
- Co-working lounge with strong Wi‑Fi if you want a calm, dry reset

## Packing List for a Quiet Wellness Trip

- Lightweight breathable clothes for humid weather
- 1 light rain jacket or compact umbrella
- Comfortable walking shoes with grip
- Sandals or slip-ons for easy temple/café visits
- 2–3 exercise or stretch outfits
- Sleepwear and one warmer layer for cool mornings
- Reusable water bottle
- Small daypack
- Sunscreen, insect repellent, and lip balm
- Personal meds and basic first aid items
- Earplugs and eye mask for rest
- Notebook or journal
- Phone charger, power bank, and universal adapter
- Swimwear if your stay has a pool or spa
- Any dietary notes in Thai or saved on your phone for vegetarian ordering

## Quiet-Trip Tips for Chiang Mai

- Choose lodging in a calm area, but not too far from vegetarian cafés and massage spots.
- Book the massage in advance for a preferred time slot.
- Keep each day to 2–3 main activities max.
- Use vegetarian-friendly phrases or save them on your phone to avoid food stress.
- Leave at least one open block each day so the retreat feels restorative, not scheduled.
